Rarity.rationale: SwordOfJade.cs:15 is RelicRarity.Event. EXECUTED (b15-pool): absent from the grab bag and named by no event -- the ONLY way to get it is relic/sword_of_stone replacing itself after five elite victories, which the b15-swords probe drives end to end (relics ['sword_of_stone'] -> ['sword_of_jade'] on the fifth elite). That matches the C# situation exactly (SwordOfStone.cs:48 is the only RelicCmd.Replace target for it), so binding rule 6's relic-side leg is satisfied via the chain. Event rarity also makes it untradable on both sides (relics/base.py:132-136).

AfterRoomEntered.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and N1 per binding rule 4. The power, the amount and the target are right and executed; the hook SITE is one dispatch later than C#'s and the applier identity differs. N1 (applier identity) is `faithful`, not an open gap -- the only live-relevant guard here is G1. LIVENESS: DORMANT, RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30 (round 11) with a REFRESHED census, since the 2026-07-26 census undercounts today's `on_combat_start` population. EXECUTED: `grep -rl 'def on_combat_start' sts2_rl/relics sts2_rl/powers.py` now returns 22 files (belt_buckle, bronze_scales, delicate_frond, ember_tea, fake_snecko_eye, fur_coat, ghost_seed, girya, gorget, kusarigama, oddly_smooth_stone, pantograph, petrified_toad [really `on_combat_start_late`], philosophers_stone, red_skull, sling_of_courage, snecko_eye, stone_cracker, sword_of_jade, tea_of_discourtesy, throwing_axe, unsettling_lamp, vajra), up from the original 14 (12 AfterRoomEntered-side + the snecko pair). Read every new file's `on_combat_start` body: `belt_buckle` (Dexterity re-arm check), `delicate_frond` (potion generation), `pantograph` (boss-room heal), `petrified_toad` (potion procurement, and its own docstring confirms its real C# hook is `BeforeCombatStartLate` -- an even LATER pass than plain `BeforeCombatStart`, so strictly after Sword of Jade regardless), `tea_of_discourtesy` (Dazed shuffle), `unsettling_lamp` (flag reset only -- its power-doubling logic lives on a different hook, `modify_power_amount`), `fur_coat` (enemy HP set), `kusarigama` (attack counter reset) -- NONE reads or is order-sensitive to the player's Strength. `philosophers_stone` grants Strength to ENEMIES only (`for enemy in self.living_enemies()`), not the player, so it cannot race Sword of Jade's self-targeted grant. The remaining Strength-granting `on_combat_start` listeners (`ember_tea`, `girya`, `vajra`, alongside `sword_of_jade` itself) are ALL on the SAME side of the C# phase split (AfterRoomEntered, per the original census, unchanged), so their mutual order is preserved on both sides and Strength addition is commutative regardless. `ruined_helmet` (the one relic that doubles the FIRST Strength gain each combat, via `modify_power_amount`, a different hook entirely) is unaffected by which of the AfterRoomEntered-side granters goes first, and still has no competing turn-start Strength source to race against. No two combat-start relics on opposite sides of the C#-phase collapse touch a shared RNG stream either. Porting a genuine C#-`BeforeCombatStart` (not `AfterRoomEntered`) relic or power that reads or scales with the player's Strength, or a wrong-stream RNG collision across the collapsed phases, would make this live; none exists today. The same guard on `relic/stone_cracker` in an earlier batch carries the same verdict for the same (now-refreshed) census, per binding rule 3.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): the C# hook is AfterRoomEntered, which runs a full dispatch BEFORE Hook.BeforeCombatStart; the port uses on_combat_start
guards.issue: POOL-WIDE SHAPE (executed census, py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-censuses): TWELVE ported relics whose C# combat effect hangs off `AfterRoomEntered` with a `room is CombatRoom` test are mapped onto the sim's on_combat_start -- bronze_scales, ember_tea, ghost_seed, girya, gorget, oddly_smooth_stone, philosophers_stone, red_skull, stone_cracker, sword_of_jade, throwing_axe, vajra -- and the sim's on_combat_start IS Hook.BeforeCombatStart, which is ONE DISPATCH LATER: CombatRoom.cs:228 fires Hook.AfterRoomEntered right after CombatManager.SetUpCombat (CombatManager.cs:350-376, which has already cloned and shuffled the draw pile via Player.PopulateCombatState, Player.cs:802-811), and only then does AfterCombatRoomLoaded -> StartCombatInternal reach Hook.BeforeCombatStart (CombatManager.cs:380-403). So C# guarantees that EVERY AfterRoomEntered relic acts before EVERY BeforeCombatStart relic, and the sim flattens both groups into one listener walk in relic-list order. This is PROMPT.md bug class 20 (right hook, wrong SITE) crossed with class 25 (a two-pass ordering guarantee destroyed by a single walk). AT THIS SITE what moves is a +3 Strength application: in C# it is guaranteed to land before every BeforeCombatStart listener, and in the sim it lands somewhere inside the single on_combat_start pass at a position decided by relic-list (acquisition) order. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, executed census): the only sim combat-start listeners that touch powers at all are the AfterRoomEntered-side relics themselves (bronze_scales, girya, gorget, oddly_smooth_stone, vajra -- all on the SAME side of the collapse, so their relative order is preserved) plus snecko_eye/fake_snecko_eye on the BeforeCombatStart side, which apply ConfusedPower and neither read nor scale with Strength. Nothing ported READS the player's Strength at combat start, and relic/ruined_helmet -- the one relic whose behaviour depends on WHICH Strength gain comes first -- has no competing combat-start Strength source to be re-ordered against (Brimstone and Demon Form are turn-start). No two combat-start relics on opposite sides of the collapse share an RNG stream either. What makes it live: porting a BeforeCombatStart relic or power that grants or reads Strength, or one that draws from a stream an AfterRoomEntered relic also uses. The same guard on relic/stone_cracker in this batch carries the same verdict for the same census (binding rule 3).

guards.what: N1: C# passes applier = NULL (SwordOfJade.cs:25); the port passes applier=self.player (sword_of_jade.py:26-29)
guards.rationale: A real argument difference, checked rather than waved through because the applier identity is load-bearing elsewhere: relic/unsettling_lamp's doubling requires `applier is self.player and target is not self.player` (unsettling_lamp.py:47) and relic/red_skull, RitualPower and the Possess powers all branch on it. EXECUTED census (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-swords, `git grep 'applier is'`): the sim has exactly four applier-branching listeners plus two docstrings -- powers.py:195 (RitualPower's `applier is not None and applier.side != owner.side` skip-first, which only fires when the power BEING applied is Ritual), powers.py:1167 (Vulnerable-only), powers.py:3094 (the Possess family's `applier is self.owner` on a NEGATIVE delta to a player-side target) and unsettling_lamp.py:47. Every one of them is unreachable for a self-targeted positive StrengthPower with applier=player: the Lamp bails because the target IS the player, Possess needs delta < 0 and applier == an enemy, Ritual needs the applied power to be Ritual, and the Vulnerable branch needs Vulnerable. relic/ruined_helmet -- the one relic that could plausibly care, since it doubles the first Strength gain -- ignores applier entirely (ruined_helmet.py:23-38 checks only power_cls, target and amount > 0), so it doubles the Jade's +3 identically either way. So the observable is unchanged today; recorded as faithful with the residual named -- any future applier-sensitive Strength listener would see a player applier where C# sees none. Rule 7: powers.py and relics/ruined_helmet.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N2: PowerVar<StrengthPower>(3m) read as BaseValue (SwordOfJade.cs:17, 25) vs STRENGTH = 3 (sword_of_jade.py:20)
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in SwordOfJade.cs, so 3 is the pinned non-ascension value. Re-read against the C# expression per PROMPT.md bug class 19 even though the port names it in a comment. EXECUTED (b15-swords): a combat with the relic opens at Strength(3). cardSource is null on both sides (the sim omits the card argument entirely), which is what keeps the Lamp out of it.

guards.what: N3: `room is CombatRoom` (SwordOfJade.cs:23) vs on_combat_start firing for every combat the sim builds
guards.rationale: The port's own docstring makes the claim ('the sim fires on_combat_start for every combat room type, so the hook maps there') and it holds: CombatState.__init__ fires hooks.on_combat_start() unconditionally (combat.py:208) and every RunState combat path -- Monster, Elite, Boss and the combat events -- goes through it, which is the same set as `room is CombatRoom`. The non-combat AfterRoomEntered rooms (EventRoom.cs:80, MerchantRoom.cs:68, RestSiteRoom.cs:37, TreasureRoom.cs:44) are excluded on both sides. Distinct from relic/sling_of_courage, whose C# AfterRoomEntered additionally filters RoomType.Elite and which therefore needs the run's room_type; this relic needs no such filter.

guards.what: N4: no state, no reset hook, no IsAllowed override; and the fact that AfterObtained is NOT overridden even though the relic arrives mid-run via RelicCmd.Replace
guards.rationale: SwordOfJade.cs declares no field and no AfterObtained; sword_of_jade.py adds nothing to __init__ and inherits the base no-op after_obtained. That matters because relic/sword_of_stone's port calls `jade.after_obtained(run)` directly (sword_of_stone.py:42) to mirror RelicCmd.Obtain's AfterObtained dispatch (RelicCmd.cs:53) -- with no override on either side that call is correctly a no-op, so the swap grants no hidden effect. PROMPT.md bug classes 13 and 16 cannot apply (no state, no IsAllowed), and `sweep-reset` / `sweep-isallowed` list the relic in no bucket -- confirmed by reading both files in full.
